thread:
emily_support: Customer reports voucher code `SPRING2026-000` being rejected as invalid/expired on checkout. Dashboard shows the code as active and expires 2026-06-01. Customer copied directly from email and pasted into checkout. Screenshot: https://redwood-screencaps.internal/xyz123
liam_billing: Can you paste the exact API response body from the browser console or network tab? Need request_id to trace.
emily_support: From customer: POST /v1/checkout/apply -> 400 {\n  \"error\": \"voucher_invalid\",\n  \"code\": \"VOUCHER_INVALID\",\n  \"request_id\": \"req_01GZ9X8YQZJ\"\n}
emily_support: Customer id `acct_78910`, org `org_442`, timestamp ~2026-03-16T15:12:43Z
zara_eng: Quick sanity check: dashboard vs API use different lookup paths. Dashboard shows the canonical voucher row, API does a normalized lookup (trim/pad). Do we have any recent migrations touching the `code` column encoding? @liam_billing
liam_billing: I queried the vouchers table for `acct_78910` vouchers. Row exists: id `v_333`, code stored as `SPRING2026` (no trailing zeros), length 10. But customer pasted `SPRING2026-000` (13 chars). Looks like legacy campaign emails appended `-000` as formatting but our API normalized to exact-match and rejected it.
zara_eng: Ah — legacy generator appended suffixes but our frontend used to strip suffixes; a change in 2025 removed tolerant normalization. Repro steps for engineering:\n```sql
SELECT id, code, LENGTH(code) as len, ENCODE(code::bytea, 'hex') as hex FROM vouchers WHERE id='v_333';
```
Also run the normalization util: `python -m rwlib.vouchers.normalize('SPRING2026-000')`
zara_eng: In my local repro, normalize currently returns `SPRING2026` for that input, but API path `apply` uses strict equality. Looks like an old codepath bypasses normalize when matching org-scoped vouchers.
emily_support: Customer says they tried removing `-000` and it worked, but they shouldn't have to edit code from email. They want either auto-accept or manual credit.
liam_billing: Issued manual credit of $50 to `acct_78910` (txn `cr_9055`). I'll add a note and make it reversible if needed. ETA: immediate.
promo-bot: [ticket created] #INC-5321 escalated to eng: `voucher-lookup-normalization`
zara_eng: Plan: 1) Patch API to accept both strict and normalized matches for 30 days; 2) Backfill DB to canonicalize codes for legacy campaigns; 3) Add unit test to prevent regression. Patch PR target: canary tomorrow 09:00 PT, full rollout by Fri EOD. We'll use rollout flag `vouchers.tolerant_lookup`.
liam_billing: I'll also run a quick audit for vouchers with suffixes: `SELECT count(*) FROM vouchers_legacy WHERE code LIKE '%-%'` and share results.
emily_support: Thanks — I'll update the customer with the manual credit and ETA. Can we also add a KB note for support: how to quickly check if code needs trimming? small snippet would help.
zara_eng: Sure — add this to KB: `if voucher contains '-' try trimming suffix after first dash and reapply` plus the SQL snippet. Will ping when PR is open.
emily_support: Great, marking resolved for now. Customer notified and credit applied. :thumbsup:
